question: After passing a Money Bill in the Lok Sabha, the Rajya Sabha can return the bill to the Lok Sabha within a maximum of ______ days. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (09/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: 28
14
22
12
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 14

Explanation:
According to Article 109 of the Indian Constitution, after a Money Bill is passed in the Lok Sabha, it is sent to the Rajya Sabha. The Rajya Sabha must return the bill to the Lok Sabha within 14 days with its recommendations. If the Rajya Sabha fails to return the bill within 14 days, it is deemed to have been passed in the form originally passed by the Lok Sabha. The Lok Sabha can accept or reject any or all of the recommendations of the Rajya Sabha. A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha and requires the prior approval of the President. The Rajya Sabha cannot amend a Money Bill; it can only make recommendations.

question: What historical decision was made based on the basic structure theory? (RPF SI 2018 (13/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Golaknath Case
Indra Sahni Case
s. R. Bomai Case
Keshavanand Bharti Case
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Keshavanand Bharti Case

Explanation:
The basic structure theory is a cornerstone of the Indian Constitution, propounded by the Supreme Court in the 1973 case of Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala. In this historic decision, the court ruled that while Parliament can amend the Constitution, it cannot destroy or alter its basic structure. This principle reinforced the supremacy of the Constitution and the power of judicial review. Before this, the Golaknath case had held that Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights, but Kesavananda Bharati overruled that view. Under this doctrine, any constitutional amendment can be struck down by the court if it violates the basic structure, which includes features like secularism, federalism, and judicial independence.

☛ In which year was the Kesavananda Bharati case decided? → 1973
☛ What was the ruling in the Golaknath case? → Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights
☛ What is included in the basic structure? → Supremacy of Constitution, judicial review, separation of powers, secularism
☛ Which case was struck down using the basic structure doctrine? → Minerva Mills case (1980)

question: The maximum limit of the Council of Ministers was fixed under which Constitutional Amendment Act? (RPF SI 2018 (13/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: 91st Constitutional Amendment
97th Constitutional Amendment
86th Constitutional Amendment
99th Constitutional Amendment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 91st Constitutional Amendment

Explanation:
The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 fixed the maximum size of the Council of Ministers. It added Articles 75(1A) and 164(1A) to the Constitution, stipulating that the total number of ministers including the Prime Minister shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha. Similarly, in states, the number of ministers including the Chief Minister cannot exceed 15% of the total members of the Legislative Assembly. This amendment aimed to control the growing number of ministers and reduce government expenditure. It came into effect in 2004.

☛ What is the maximum number of ministers including Prime Minister? → 15% of Lok Sabha members
☛ Which article limits the Council of Ministers in states? → Article 164(1A)

question: The word "Primus inter Pares" shows which of the following? (RPF SI 2018 (13/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: President
Home Minister
Prime Minister
Cabinet Minister
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Prime Minister

Explanation:
The Latin phrase "Primus inter Pares" translates to "first among equals." It describes a person who is the leader or foremost among a group of peers, without possessing superior legal authority over them. In a parliamentary system, the Prime Minister is often considered the "first among equals" within the cabinet. The Prime Minister is a member of the cabinet like other ministers, but as the head of government, holds a preeminent position. According to this concept, the Prime Minister is the leading figure among equals, not a superior authority. Unlike a President or head of state, the Prime Minister's power is based on the collective responsibility of the cabinet. This term is used in political science to explain the nature of government where the leader is not above others but primus among them. It applies to many countries following the Westminster system, such as India and the United Kingdom.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Which language does this term originate from? → Latin
☛ For which position is this term used in India? → Prime Minister
☛ How does the Prime Minister relate to the cabinet in a parliamentary system? → As first among equals
☛ Which type of government system uses this concept? → Westminster system (e.g., India, UK)

लैटिन भाषा का शब्द "प्राइमस इंटर पारेस" (Primus inter Pares) का अर्थ है "समानों में प्रथम" या "बराबरों में पहला"। यह शब्द उस व्यक्ति को दर्शाता है जो अपने समूह में समान स्तर के लोगों के बीच अग्रणी होता है, परंतु उसके पास अन्य सदस्यों पर कोई विशेष कानूनी अधिकार नहीं होता। संसदीय प्रणाली में, प्रधान मंत्री को इसी रूप में देखा जाता है। प्रधान मंत्री कैबिनेट में अन्य मंत्रियों के समान ही एक सदस्य है, लेकिन सरकार का मुखिया होने के नाते वह सर्वोपरि स्थान रखता है। इस अवधारणा के अनुसार, प्रधान मंत्री अपने मंत्रिमंडल में "समानों में प्रथम" होता है, न कि उनसे श्रेष्ठ। राष्ट्रपति या राज्य प्रमुख के विपरीत, प्रधान मंत्री की शक्ति कैबिनेट की सामूहिक जिम्मेदारी पर आधारित होती है। यह शब्द राजनीति विज्ञान में सरकार के स्वरूप को समझाने के लिए प्रयुक्त होता है।

question: The provisions related to the federal structure of the state system given in the Constitution can be modified by whom?  (RPF SI 2018 (13/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Constitutional frame time for voting only for Union Ministers
Special Parliament only in Parliament
Special majority in Parliament with the consent of half of the state legislatures by a simple majority
Effective majority in parliament
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Special majority in Parliament with the consent of half of the state legislatures by a simple majority

Explanation:
The provisions related to the federal structure of the state system in the Indian Constitution, such as changes to state boundaries, names, or territories, can be amended under Article 368 through a special procedure. This requires a special majority in Parliament, meaning a majority of the total membership of each House and at least two-thirds of the members present and voting. Additionally, at least half of the state legislatures must give their consent by passing the bill with a simple majority. This process safeguards the federal structure and ensures states' involvement in major constitutional changes.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which Article provides for amendment of federal structure? → Article 368
☛ What majority is required in Parliament for such amendments? → Special majority (two-thirds of members present and voting plus majority of total membership)
☛ How many states must consent? → At least half of the states
☛ What majority is needed in state legislatures for consent? → Simple majority
☛ Is state consent mandatory for federal structure amendments? → Yes

question: Which British Government got autonomy for the provinces by reforming?  (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Government of India Act, 1935
Government of India Act, 1909
Government of India Act, 1919
Queen's Proclamation in 1858
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Government of India Act, 1935

Explanation:
The Government of India Act, 1935 was a landmark legislation passed by the British Parliament that granted provincial autonomy. This act abolished dyarchy at the provincial level and introduced responsible government in the provinces, where ministers were accountable to the legislature. It provided provinces with powers to legislate and levy taxes, making them largely independent in internal affairs. The act also envisioned a federal structure for India, though the federal part was never implemented. This act was a significant step in the constitutional development of India and paved the way for future governance reforms. It marked a shift from centralized control to more decentralized provincial administration.

question: Which court in India is responsible for handling civil cases like property disputes, divorce and consumer problems? (RPF Constable 2024 (18/03/2025) Shift 1)

question: What is the maximum number of Ministers allowed in the Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, as per the 91st Amendment Act? (RRB JE ECE (22/04/2025) Shift 1 CBT 2)
options: 12% of Lok Sabha strength
10% of Lok Sabha strength
15% of Lok Sabha strength
20% of Lok Sabha strength
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 15% of Lok Sabha strength

Explanation:
The 91st Amendment Act, 2003, amended Articles 75 and 164 of the Indian Constitution. It stipulates that the total number of ministers in the Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, shall not exceed 15% of the total membership of the Lok Sabha. This provision was made to limit the size of the cabinet and ensure efficient governance. For example, with the current Lok Sabha having 543 members, the maximum number of ministers would be 81 (15% of 543). This amendment is crucial for political stability and accountability. Similarly, in states, the number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, cannot exceed 15% of the total members of the Legislative Assembly, but must have a minimum of 12 ministers.

question_hi: 91वें संशोधन अधिनियम के अनुसार, मंत्रिपरिषद में प्रधानमंत्री सहित मंत्रियों की अधिकतम संख्या कितनी है? (RRB JE ECE (22/04/2025) Shift 1 CBT 2)

question: Free legal aid is part of which part of the Indian Constitution? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (06/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Directive Principles
Fundamental Rights
Fundamental Duties
Preamble
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Directive Principles

Explanation:
Part IV of the Indian Constitution contains the Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 36-51). Article 39A directs the State to provide free legal aid to ensure equal justice and equal opportunity. This principle is not enforceable by courts but is fundamental in the governance of the country. It aims to ensure access to justice for the poor and weaker sections of society. Free legal aid is not a Fundamental Right under the Directive Principles; however, the Supreme Court has later held it to be part of Article 21 (Right to Life) as a Fundamental Right. Thus, free legal aid is primarily enshrined in the Directive Principles of State Policy.

question: What is the Gram Sabha in the context of the Panchayati Raj system in India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (06/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: An advisory council of State representatives
The deliberative assembly of all eligible village residents
A judicial body for urban areas
A block-level committee
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The deliberative assembly of all eligible village residents

Explanation:
Gram Sabha is the foundational body of the Panchayati Raj system, consisting of all eligible voters (usually persons aged 18 years and above) of a village. It is a deliberative assembly, not an executive or judicial body. The Gram Sabha discusses and approves the plans and budget of the Gram Panchayat. The 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to the Gram Sabha. It ensures transparency and accountability by overseeing the functioning of the Gram Panchayat. The Gram Sabha must meet at least twice a year. Its primary role is to discuss and approve development plans, select beneficiaries, and audit the Gram Panchayat's accounts.

question: Who among the following is the political head of the municipality in India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (17/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Chief Municipal Officer
Chairman
Mayor
Municipal Commissioner
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chairman

Explanation:
In India, the political head of the Municipality is the Chairman. A Municipality is an urban local body found in smaller towns. Its head is an elected representative, known as the Chairman or President. The Mayor is the head of a Municipal Corporation, which exists in larger cities. Chief Municipal Officer and Municipal Commissioner are administrative officers, not political heads. The 74th Constitutional Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to municipalities. The Chairman presides over council meetings and plays a key role in policy decisions.

question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन भारत में नगरपालिका का राजनीतिक प्रमुख है? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (17/06/2025) Shift 3)

अध्यक्ष
महापौर
नगर आयुक्त
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अध्यक्ष

Explanation:
भारत में नगरपालिका का राजनीतिक प्रमुख अध्यक्ष होता है। नगरपालिका एक नगरीय स्थानीय निकाय है जो छोटे शहरों में पाया जाता है। इसका प्रमुख निर्वाचित जनप्रतिनिधि होता है, जिसे अध्यक्ष या सभापति कहा जाता है। महापौर निगम (नगर निगम) का प्रमुख होता है, जो बड़े शहरों में होता है। मुख्य नगरपालिका अधिकारी और नगर आयुक्त प्रशासनिक अधिकारी होते हैं, राजनीतिक प्रमुख नहीं। 74वें संविधान संशोधन (1992) ने नगरपालिकाओं को संवैधानिक दर्जा दिया। अध्यक्ष नगरपालिका की बैठकों की अध्यक्षता करता है और नीतिगत निर्णय लेने में भूमिका निभाता है।
